Recall that the catalyst is vanadium(V) oxide with formula $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$, not iron which belongs to the Haber process.
Use the rule that oxygen is -2 to work out the oxidation number of vanadium in $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$ and see which row matches both parts.
walkthrough:
**Recall the Contact process**

Great start, let us place the reaction. The Contact process oxidises sulfur dioxide to sulfur trioxide:
$$2\text{SO}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3$$
This needs a catalyst to get a good rate at about 450 degrees C.

**Identify the catalyst**

This is a classic learn-it fact. The catalyst is vanadium(V) oxide, $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$. Iron is the catalyst for a different process, the Haber process for ammonia, so we can rule out iron here.

**Calculate the oxidation number of vanadium**

Let the oxidation number of V be $x$. Oxygen is almost always -2.
$$2x + 5(-2) = 0$$
$$2x - 10 = 0$$
$$x = +5$$
So we need element vanadium with oxidation number +5.

options.A: Incorrect. Iron as $\text{Fe}$ with oxidation number 0 is the catalyst for the Haber process ($\text{N}_2 + 3\text{H}_2$), not the Contact process.
options.B: Incorrect. Iron is wrong for the Contact process. Oxidation number +3 would fit $\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3$, but that compound is not used here. This mixes up Haber and Contact catalysts.
options.C: Incorrect. Vanadium is the right element, but 0 is wrong. The catalyst is a compound, $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$, not free vanadium metal, so vanadium must have a positive oxidation number.
options.D: Correct. The Contact process uses vanadium(V) oxide, $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$. With O at -2, vanadium is at +5, giving element vanadium and oxidation number +5.
